answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from stake-weighted admission to a shared work pool. Each agent posts a nontransferable bond that a slashing rule can burn, and reputation earned in one orchard of tasks cannot be cloned into fresh keys. An attacker who spins up a thousand identities must fund a thousand bonds; if the pool only lifts one plume of influence above a fixed tide of capital, the cost scales linearly while the payoff stays flat, so forgery stops paying.
